selected_topic.title: Félix Carvajal: the Olympic marathoner who hitchhiked to the start
selected_topic.angle: A Cuban runner lost his travel money gambling, hitchhiked to St. Louis, arrived in improvised race clothes, stopped for apples, and still finished fourth in the 1904 Olympic marathon.
selected_topic.viewer_value: A comic sequence of setbacks turns into a compact story of resourcefulness and persistence, while revealing how strange and hazardous the 1904 Olympic marathon was.

sources.claim: Carvajal ran across Cuba to raise travel money, lost it gambling in New Orleans, hitchhiked to St. Louis, wore street clothes altered by Martin Sheridan, ate green apples during the marathon, and finished fourth.
The race took place in 33°C heat on dusty, hilly roads; only one water station was set up; Carvajal stopped to eat apples and finished fourth.
Fred Lorz was first across the line after taking a car ride, and eventual winner Thomas Hicks received egg whites, brandy and strychnine sulphate during the race.

audience_assumption: English-speaking general audience, including viewers unfamiliar with early Olympic history; no specialist background assumed.

shortlist_and_decision.candidate: Félix Carvajal at the 1904 Olympic marathon
shortlist_and_decision.hook: He lost his Olympic travel money gambling, then hitchhiked to the race.
shortlist_and_decision.development: Improvised clothes, apples and cramps, keeps running.
shortlist_and_decision.payoff: Fourth place despite the chain of setbacks; start line itself becomes the story.
shortlist_and_decision.objection: Early Olympic marathon anecdotes are a known genre; avoid turning the runner into a joke.

shortlist_and_decision.hook: A city street was hit by a fast-moving wave of molasses.
shortlist_and_decision.development: Tank failure, dangerous cleanup and investigation.
shortlist_and_decision.objection: Widely repeated online, and the spectacle can flatten a deadly disaster into novelty.

shortlist_and_decision.candidate: Fred Lorz car ride in the same marathon
shortlist_and_decision.hook: A runner appeared to win an Olympic marathon after riding in a car.
shortlist_and_decision.development: He dropped out, took a ride, then ran the last miles.
shortlist_and_decision.payoff: Disqualification; the eventual winner was near collapse.
shortlist_and_decision.objection: A one-beat hoax story, with less emotional progression than Carvajal longer arc.

selection_rationale: Carvajal has a concrete opening problem, escalating reversals, and a satisfying outcome. It beats the adjacent Lorz story because persistence supplies a full character arc, and beats the molasses story for this brief because it can deliver humor and admiration without making a mass-casualty event a novelty gag.

This does not establish every anecdote through a primary 1904 source. Avoid invented dialogue, precise distances, or claims about exactly how far he hitchhiked.
